title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Coordinate System Basics
text:
Coordinate System Basics

Key terms: coordinate system, grid-based thinking, Baudhāyana-Pythagoras Theorem

A coordinate system is a framework using numbers to describe exact locations. It has deep roots in ancient civilizations like the Sindhu-Sarasvatī Civilisation and was developed further by mathematicians like Baudhāyana, Ptolemy, and Brahmagupta.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Coordinate System Basics in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Cartesian Coordinate System
text:
Cartesian Coordinate System

Key terms: Cartesian coordinate system, x-axis, y-axis, origin

The Cartesian coordinate system uses two perpendicular axes (x-axis and y-axis) to locate points in a two-dimensional plane. The point of intersection is called the origin (O).

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Cartesian Coordinate System in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Quadrants and Coordinates
text:
Quadrants and Coordinates

Key terms: quadrant, coordinates, sign of coordinates

The plane is divided into four quadrants by the axes. The coordinates of a point in the plane represent its perpendicular distances from the axes. The sign of the coordinates indicates the quadrant.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Quadrants and Coordinates in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Distance Between Two Points
text:
Distance Between Two Points

Key terms: distance formula, Baudhāyana-Pythagoras Theorem

The distance between two points in the plane can be found using the Baudhāyana-Pythagoras Theorem. It's calculated as the square root of the sum of the squares of the differences in their x and y coordinates.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Distance Between Two Points in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Reflection of a Triangle
text:
Reflection of a Triangle

Key terms: reflection, axis, side lengths

Reflecting a triangle across an axis preserves the lengths of its sides, but changes the direction of the sides.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Reflection of a Triangle in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Intersection of Axes
text:
Intersection of Axes

Key terms: origin, intersection, axes

The intersection of the x-axis and y-axis is the origin, where both coordinates are zero.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Intersection of Axes in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Parallel Lines and Axes
text:
Parallel Lines and Axes

Lines parallel to the axes have the same x-coordinate or y-coordinate for all points on the line.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Parallel Lines and Axes in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Perpendicular Lines and Axes
text:
Perpendicular Lines and Axes

Lines perpendicular to the axes have a slope of 0 or undefined, respectively.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Perpendicular Lines and Axes in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Midpoint of a Segment
text:
Midpoint of a Segment

The midpoint of a segment has coordinates that are the average of the coordinates of the segment's endpoints.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Midpoint of a Segment in Grade 9 Mathematics.

Distance Between Two Points

The distance between two points can be found using the distance formula, which involves the difference in their x and y coordinates.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Distance Between Two Points in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Circle with Origin as Center
text:

A circle with the origin as its center has a radius equal to the distance from the origin to any point on the circle.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Circle with Origin as Center in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Street Intersections in a City
text:
Street Intersections in a City

Street intersections in a city can be represented using coordinates, with the number of streets in the North-South direction and East-West direction as the coordinates.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Street Intersections in a City in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Linear Polynomials Definition
text:
Linear Polynomials Definition

Key terms: linear polynomial, univariate, polynomial

Linear polynomials are algebraic expressions involving one variable and its powers, with the highest power being 1. They are also called univariate polynomials or just polynomials.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Linear Polynomials Definition in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Degree of a Polynomial
text:
Degree of a Polynomial

Key terms: degree, polynomial

The degree of a polynomial is the highest power of the variable present in the polynomial. For example, in 5x^3 + 2x^2 - 3x + 4, the degree is 3.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Degree of a Polynomial in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Linear Polynomials in Real-life Situations
text:
Linear Polynomials in Real-life Situations

Key terms: real-life situation, linear polynomial

Linear polynomials can represent real-life situations where a quantity changes at a constant rate, like the perimeter of a square or the cost of a journey.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Linear Polynomials in Real-life Situations in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Linear Equations from Polynomials
text:
Linear Equations from Polynomials

Key terms: linear equation, polynomial

When a linear polynomial is equated to a constant, it results in a linear equation. For example, 2x + 3 = 7 is a linear equation.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Linear Equations from Polynomials in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Polynomials as Input-Output Processes
text:
Polynomials as Input-Output Processes

Key terms: input, output, polynomial

A polynomial can be thought of as an input-output process, where the input is the value of the variable and the output is the value of the polynomial.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Polynomials as Input-Output Processes in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Linear Growth and Decay
text:
Linear Growth and Decay

Key terms: linear growth, linear decay, constant amount

Linear growth describes a pattern where a quantity increases by a constant amount over equal intervals. Similarly, linear decay describes a pattern where a quantity decreases by a constant amount over equal intervals.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Linear Growth and Decay in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Linear Relationships
text:
Linear Relationships

Key terms: linear relationship, slope, y-intercept

A linear relationship between two variables x and y can be expressed as y = ax + b, where 'a' represents the slope of the line and 'b' represents the y-intercept.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Linear Relationships in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Linear Equations
text:
Linear Equations

Key terms: linear equation, polynomial, degree

A linear equation is a polynomial equation of degree 1, which can be written in the form y = ax + b, where 'a' and 'b' are constants.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Linear Equations in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Graphing Linear Equations
text:
Graphing Linear Equations

Key terms: graph, linear equation, straight line

To graph a linear equation, we need to identify at least two points on the line and plot them on the coordinate plane. The graph of a linear equation is a straight line.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Graphing Linear Equations in Grade 9 Mathematics.

To convert Kelvin to Fahrenheit, use the formula (K - 273.15) * 9/5 + 32.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Temperature Conversion: Kelvin to Fahrenheit in Grade 9 Mathematics.

text:

To convert Fahrenheit to Kelvin, use the formula (F - 32) * 5/9 + 273.15.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Temperature Conversion: Fahrenheit to Kelvin in Grade 9 Mathematics.

text:
Work Done by a Constant Force

Work done (W) is the product of constant force (F) and distance (d) in the direction of the force: W = F * d.

metadata.topic: Work Done by a Constant Force

A linear polynomial in two variables is of the form p(x) = ax + b, where a and b are constants.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Graph of a Linear Polynomial
text:
Graph of a Linear Polynomial

Key terms: graph, linear, polynomial

The graph of a linear polynomial p(x) = ax + b is a straight line that passes through the points (0, b) and (1/a, b + 1).

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Graph of a Linear Polynomial in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Growing Pattern of Hexagons
text:

The number of matchsticks required for the nth stage of the hexagon pattern is given by the formula 6n^2 - 9n + 7.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Growing Pattern of Hexagons in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Parallel Linear Polynomials
text:

Two linear polynomials p(x) = ax + b and q(x) = ax + d are parallel if and only if a = c and b ≠ d.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Parallel Linear Polynomials in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Linear Functions with a Common Form
text:
Linear Functions with a Common Form

Key terms: linear, function, common form

All linear functions of the form f(x) = ax + a, where a > 0, have a y-intercept of (0, a) and pass through the origin (0, 0).

metadata.topic: Linear Functions with a Common Form
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Linear Functions with a Common Form in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | One-to-One Correspondence
text:
One-to-One Correspondence

Key terms: one-to-one correspondence, natural numbers

Early humans used one-to-one correspondence to count, matching objects to ensure nothing was missing. This concept led to the birth of natural numbers.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to One-to-One Correspondence in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Earliest Evidence of Counting
text:
Earliest Evidence of Counting

Key terms: Lebombo Bone, Ishango Bone, tally marks, prime numbers

The Lebombo and Ishango bones, dating back thousands of years, show early humans using tally marks to record numbers, indicating a basic understanding of counting and even prime numbers.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Earliest Evidence of Counting in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Indian Context: Trade and Astronomy
text:
Indian Context: Trade and Astronomy

Ancient Indian civilizations used a robust system of accounting for trade and had a deep fascination with large numbers, setting the stage for the development of the number system based on powers of 10.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Indian Context: Trade and Astronomy in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Concept of Zero
text:
Concept of Zero

Key terms: zero, emptiness, Brahmagupta

Indian philosophers' reverence for the state of 'emptiness' led to the mathematical concept of zero, which was formally defined and operationalized by Brahmagupta.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Concept of Zero in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Negative Numbers
text:
Negative Numbers

Brahmagupta introduced negative numbers to represent debts, expanding the number line to include integers (positive, negative, and zero).

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Negative Numbers in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Arithmetic of Integers
text:

Brahmagupta provided rules for adding and multiplying integers, which are still used today, including the concept that a negative times a negative equals a positive.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Arithmetic of Integers in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Fractions and Rational Numbers
text:

Key terms: fractions, rational numbers, closure under operations

As society grew more complex, measuring led to the need for fractions. Rational numbers include all integers and fractions, and they are closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division (except by zero).

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Fractions and Rational Numbers in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Rational Numbers on the Number Line
text:
Rational Numbers on the Number Line

Key terms: rational number, number line, absolute value

Rational numbers can be represented on the number line by dividing the unit interval into equal parts and moving a certain number of parts from 0. The absolute value of a rational number is its distance from 0.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.topic: Rational Numbers on the Number Line
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Rational Numbers on the Number Line in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Density of Rational Numbers
text:

Key terms: dense, rational numbers, average

Rational numbers are dense on the number line, meaning there is always another rational number between any two rational numbers. The average of two rational numbers is also a rational number.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Density of Rational Numbers in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Irrational Numbers
text:
Irrational Numbers

Key terms: irrational number, proof by contradiction, √2, π

Irrational numbers are numbers that cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers. They are proven to be irrational using proof by contradiction. Examples include √2 and π.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Irrational Numbers in Grade 9 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Constructing Irrational Lengths
text:

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Constructing Irrational Lengths in Grade 9 Mathematics.

metadata.topic: Real Numbers: Decimals and Cyclic Patterns

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Geometric Progression (GP) Formula
text:
Geometric Progression (GP) Formula

Key terms: geometric progression, common ratio, formula

The 'n'th term of a geometric progression is given by the formula ar^(n-1), where 'a' is the first term and 'r' is the common ratio.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Sequence Recursive Formula
text:
Sequence Recursive Formula

Key terms: sequence, recursive formula, Fibonacci

A recursive formula for a sequence uses the values of previous terms to calculate the value of a given term. For example, the recursive formula for the Fibonacci sequence is F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2).

title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Explicit Formula for a Sequence
text:
Explicit Formula for a Sequence

Key terms: sequence, explicit formula, triangular number

An explicit formula for a sequence uses the term's position number 'n' to calculate the term's value. For example, the explicit formula for the 'n'th triangular number is n(n + 1)/2.
